title: Measuring AI Agents' Progress on Multi-Step Cyber Attack Scenarios
abstract: arXiv:2603.11214v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We evaluate the autonomous offensive cyber capabilities of frontier AI agents on two purpose-built cyber ranges---a 32-step corporate network attack and a 7-step industrial control system attack targeting a simulated cooling tower---complemented by a private 76-task CTF suite spanning four difficulty tiers. Human-expert solve times are estimated at roughly 20 hours for the corporate range and 15 hours for the cooling tower; CTF time annotations range from 1 minute to over 42 hours and include measured playtests, designer estimates, and lower bounds from unsolved playtests. Across thirteen models released over a twenty-month period---from GPT-4o in August 2024 to GPT-5.5 in April 2026---we observe two trends. First, step-count progress increases approximately log-linearly with inference-time compute over the tested range (up to 100M tokens). tldr: 该研究通过两个定制网络靶场和76个CTF任务系统评估了十三款前沿AI模型的自主网络攻击能力，发现攻击步数进展随推理时计算量大致呈对数线性增长，且更新的模型在固定token预算下能完成更多攻击步骤。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates the autonomous offensive cyber capabilities of thirteen frontier AI models using two purpose-built cyber ranges and a 76-task CTF suite, finding that step-count progress scales approximately log-linearly with inference-time compute, and newer models complete more attack steps at fixed token budgets.
